question.text: Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) in India are regulated by which authority?

answer.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

explanation.text: The Logic: Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) are pooled investment vehicles that hold income-generating real estate and issue units that are listed on stock exchanges. Because REIT units are securities offered to and traded by public investors, their issuance, listing, and ongoing disclosures fall within the securities-market regulator's remit. In India, that regulator is SEBI, which has issued and continues to administer the SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014 governing registration, structure, sponsor/manager obligations, distributions, and listing. The Trap: RBI is the central bank and regulates banking, monetary policy, and certain NBFCs - not listed pooled investment vehicles. IRDAI regulates insurance companies and intermediaries. NHB historically regulates housing finance companies on the lending side, not real-estate-backed pooled investment trusts. None of these regulate the issuance or trading of REIT units, which is a securities-market function. Note: The cited workbook pages (34-35, 43, 45, 194-197 of the NISM Series XV Research Analyst workbook) define REITs and InvITs and mention their regulatory and structural requirements but do not, in the pages checked, explicitly name SEBI as the REIT regulator or cite the SEBI REIT Regulations. The framing above reflects general regulatory knowledge - REITs in India are in fact governed by the SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014.
